newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania referendum shows just 33.3 pct backed king.
newsitem.headline: Albania referendum shows just 33.3 pct backed king.

text.p: Albanians overwhelmingly rejected restoring the monarchy in a June 29 referendum held during general elections designed to restore stability in the Balkan country, state television reported on Monday.
The television quoted an electoral commission statement that put the final vote for the monarchy at 33.26 percent versus 66.74 percent in favour of remaining a republic.
Self-proclaimed King Leka I arrived in Albania from his South African home in April amid a violent rebellion sparked by the collapse of pyramid savings schemes that have left over 1,500 dead.
The 58-year-old lays claim to the throne left vacant since his father King Zog fled Albania in 1939 before Mussolini's troops invaded.

Preliminary results after the referendum had shown a similar outcome. The would-be king says the result was manipulated. He left the country on Saturday for his South African home, promising to return.
However, election observers reported no serious problems with the vote and Leka's supporters have so far produced little evidence of fraud.
Diplomats said even 33 percent support seemed high, calling the result as much a protest against President Sali Berisha as a vote for the king.
Ex-communists won a landslide victory over Berisha's Democratic Party in the June 29 elections.
